chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Abi Ja'far al-Muqarri, who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him), on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers (peace be upon them).

He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Five things upon which a judge must rule based on what is apparent: leadership (al-wilayah), marriage (al-munakih), inheritance (al-mawarith), offerings/sacrifices (al-dhaba'ih), and testimonies (al-shahadat). When the apparent state of the witnesses is trustworthy, their testimony is valid and they are not questioned about their inward reality.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five circumstances where a judge rules based on apparent evidence rather than inner reality?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal articulates the jurisprudential principle of 'al-zuhur bi al-zahir' (relying on the apparent), where judges rule based on visible evidence rather than exhaustive investigation of inner truth, provided witnesses are deemed trustworthy. This approach ensures legal efficiency and social stability by preventing endless scrutiny of individuals' hidden states in matters of leadership, marriage, inheritance, sacrifices, and testimonies. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical legal certainty over metaphysical perfection in judicial proceedings.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-89 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Abi Ja’far al-Muqar’ri who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB)

that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said, “A judge must rule based on what is apparent in five circumstances: the question of leadership; marriage; inheritance; the offerings; the testimonies - once those who bear witness appear to be upright he must accept their testimony and should not investigate about their inward things.”
